messages:
Samira Chen: paging — p99 token latency for infer-runtime (us-west1) jumped from ~220ms to ~480ms after this morning's rolling deploy. Canary shift happened ~12m ago. Seeing kernel-fallback spikes and batch sizes drop to 1.
incident-bot: ALERT: High latency on service=infer-runtime env=prod region=us-west1 — triggered p99>400ms across multiple pods. PagerDuty: https://p.d/REDACTED/inc9876 :rotating_light:
deploy-bot: deploy v1.3.0 (sha=abc123def) -> prod. Canary traffic: 60% shifted at 11:03 UTC. Rollout started by jpark.
Jesse Park: I pushed the prefetch/batching change in v1.3.0 — it's supposed to prefetch KV keys earlier and increase batch coalescing. Not expecting kernel fallback though. Can someone share memory/eviction stats?
Arun Patel (eng-platform): pulling pod metrics now. KV-cache miss rate spiked and memory pressure on a subset of pods. Suspect prefetch warmed large keys causing cache thrash and LRU churn.
Priya Nair (eng-sre): this matches traces — when cache thrash happens runtime is evicting KV pages and falling back to reference kernels, which kills throughput and increases p99.
Samira Chen: can we flip the prefetch feature flag for prod? If turning it off reduces pressure we can pause the rollout.
Samira Chen: flipping feature flag prefetch_v2 -> OFF via console now.
deploy-bot: feature-flag prefetch_v2 set to OFF by Samira Chen at 11:18 UTC.
Liam O'Connor: seeing p99 drop to ~260ms on most pods but throughput still lower than baseline. A handful of pods still in kernel-fallback state.
Jesse Park: looks like some pods are stuck with older kernel tables and won't recover until we restart or rollback. I'm leaning toward rollback to v1.2.8 (stable). Thoughts?
Priya Nair (eng-sre): agree. Kill-switch helped but not fully. Rolling rollback will restore baseline kernels without requiring pod restarts en masse. We should coordinate with platform for a safe rollback window.
Samira Chen: initiating rollback to v1.2.8. Rollback because partial kernel state + KV thrash is causing throughput to drop even after flag flip.
deploy-bot: rollback to v1.2.8 triggered by Samira Chen at 11:28 UTC. Rollout controller: starting undo.
Samira Chen: steps I'm running: 1) rollback via rollout undo 2) restart 4 pods still reporting kernel_fallback_count>0 3) monitor p95/p99 and token throughput 4) update CS + product.
Samira Chen: kubectl command I'm using:
```
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/infer-runtime --to-revision=202 
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=infer-runtime -o wide
kubectl -n prod delete pod <podname> 
```
Arun Patel (eng-platform): I pushed a targeted restart action for the 4 stuck pods to avoid full cluster churn. Restart done at 11:34 UTC.
support-bot: CS alert created: incident_id=INC-2026, severity=P2, affected_customers=[acme-inc, ledgerize, finovate]. Ticket links: https://support/INC-2026
Maya Singh (CS): notified top customers via the support playbook. Messaging: brief outage-like degradation for token latency and throughput in us-west1; engineers rolling back.
Priya Nair (eng-sre): dumping a quick KV cache stat snapshot from one affected pod:
```
{
  "pod": "infer-runtime-7f9b",
  "kv_cache_size": "1.2GB",
  "kv_cache_miss_rate": "18%",
  "kernel_fallback_count": "42",
  "uptime": "2h"
}
```
Jesse Park: thanks. kernel_fallback_count confirms runtime switched to slow path repeatedly. That matches the batch_size=1 events in traces. Prefetch warmed oversized entries and caused thrash.
Liam O'Connor: rollback progressing — controller reports 40% -> 100% to v1.2.8 by 11:45 UTC. Throughput trending back toward baseline.
Samira Chen: p99 now ~210-250ms across the board. Throughput still recovering to normal QPS — hitting 80% of baseline. Will continue monitoring.
Priya Nair (eng-sre): handoff: I'm taking on-call from Samira in 20m. Samira — can you summarize actions for my notes? Also add whether any mitigation required customer-facing postures?
Samira Chen: summary for handoff: 1) root cause: prefetch_v2 in v1.3.0 caused KV-cache thrash -> kernel fallback -> batch collapse -> p99 spike + throughput drop. 2) immediate mitigations: feature flag OFF, rollback to v1.2.8, targeted pod restarts. 3) impact: transient P2 degradation, degraded throughput and increased tail latency in us-west1 for ~25 minutes; affected customers notified. 4) next steps: preserve logs, collect full traces for the 11:00-11:40 window, schedule postmortem with eng-runtime + eng-sre + platform.
Maya Singh (CS): logging customer comms and holding follow-ups for any escalations. No SLA breaches expected but monitoring open.
Arun Patel (eng-platform): arch note — we'll add a health-check for kernel fallback count and fail early in the rollout controller if > threshold. Also propose a canary check for kv-cache miss rate before increasing traffic.
Jesse Park: I'll revert the prefetch change branch and run a more conservative prefetch prototype in staging. We should also add a flag that prefetches only small keys.
Priya Nair (eng-sre): writing incident ticket & assigning postmortem owners. Estimated incident severity P2.
Samira Chen: handing off to Priya for next 2 hours. Priya please post a final update when we have full traffic and tail metrics normalized. :white_check_mark:
Priya Nair (eng-sre): taking handoff. I'll keep this channel updated. If anyone sees new spikes, ping @pagerduty.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: rollback complete, latency trending to baseline, incident status: under control.
Samira Chen: thanks team — great coordination. We'll follow up with a short postmortem and remediation plan tomorrow. :heart:
